pr_title: driver: mission executor with claim lease, read-back and scoped inbox (#483)
title: Require receipt-write capability before executing missions
body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require receipt-write capability before executing missions**

With a token scoped only to `read_missions`, this path executes the action before `write_receipt()` rejects the missing capability. The mission remains queued and its claim remains `claimed`, so polling again with the same owner executes the action again. This is reproducible on consecutive `run()` calls without waiting for lease expiry. Require both executor capabilities before claiming or executing any mission so a known inability to file receipts cannot leave completed actions replayable.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: driver_core/mission_executor.py: `process_next` claims and calls `self.execute(mission)` with no capability check; `write_receipts` is required only inside `MissionInbox.write_receipt` (line 276), so a read-only token executes first and the claim stays `claimed`.

pr_title: driver: mission executor with claim lease, read-back and scoped inbox (#483)
title: Handle unreadable mission payloads inside the refusal path
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle unreadable mission payloads inside the refusal path**

When the oldest `.json` mission contains malformed JSON, an oversized payload, or a non-mapping value, `inbox.read()` raises before entering the refusal handler. Consequently, `run()` aborts without parking or receipting that mission, and every subsequent poll encounters the same file instead of processing later valid missions. Catch these per-mission read refusals and use the validated filename as the fallback receipt identity so a bad payload does not permanently block the queue.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: driver_core/mission_executor.py:508 `payload = self.inbox.read(filename)` runs before the `try` that catches `MissionRefused`, so malformed, oversized or non-mapping payloads abort `process_next` without a receipt or park.

pr_title: driver: mission executor with claim lease, read-back and scoped inbox (#483)
title: Validate inbox directories against the declared root
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate inbox directories against the declared root**

If `root/missions` is a symlink to an external directory, the parent comparison succeeds because both sides resolve to that external directory, while `islink(path)` checks only the mission file itself. The executor therefore reads, executes, and removes missions outside the declared private root; this is reproducible with an ordinary JSON file beneath a symlinked `missions` directory. Validate the directory itself against the root and reject symlinked inbox directories; the same directory helper also allows receipts and archives to be redirected outside the root.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: driver_core/mission_executor.py:208 `_directory()` joins and creates the path with no root or symlink check; `_mission_path` line 224 tests `os.path.islink(path)` on the file only, so a symlinked `missions/` reads and removes files outside the declared root.

pr_title: answer lifecycle: hold a delivered plotting script to its own claims (#568)
title: Resolve bar positions before reporting a tick-unit mismatch
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve bar positions before reporting a tick-unit mismatch**

For a valid script using `xs = [10 ** k for k in range(3)]`, `ax.bar(xs, heights)`, and matching power-of-ten ticks, this check reports that `xs` does not contain powers of ten. `_record_call` adds every named bar-position argument to `plain_bar_positions` without inspecting its value, so the finding is unsupported even when positions and ticks match exactly. The lifecycle consequently spends a revision and withholds a correct script if the generator preserves those positions. Resolve the position values and associate them with the relevant axes before asserting a mismatch.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/answer_plot_consistency.py:219 and :299 append every named bar-position argument to `plain_bar_positions` without resolving its value; finding (3) at :419 reports a tick-unit mismatch whenever power ticks exist.

title: Preserve branch conditions for argparse namespace attributes
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve branch conditions for argparse namespace attributes**

For the standard argparse pattern `args = parser.parse_args()` followed by `if args.log:`, `_flag_of` does not recognize the attribute expression, so both branches are collected with identical conditions. A correct toggle that sets a log scale and title in one branch and a linear scale and title in the other therefore produces contradictory `panel-title` findings in every checked state. This causes correct toggle answers to be revised and potentially withheld. Track namespace flag attributes, and do not treat mutually exclusive branches as simultaneously executed when their condition is unresolved.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/answer_plot_consistency.py:148 `_flag_of` resolves `ast.Name` and aliases only; an `ast.Attribute` such as `args.log` yields None, so both argparse branches collect with identical conditions.

title: Compare panel titles against the effective final scale
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare panel titles against the effective final scale**

If a script initializes an axis with `ax.set_xscale("linear")` and later switches it to `"log"` before display, a `"Log scale"` title is correct, but this loop reports the earlier linear setter as a contradiction. It compares the title against every setter rather than the final effective setting, so even an unconditional, statically resolvable initialization followed by an override can cause a correct answer to be withheld. Derive the final scale for each axis dimension and state before comparing it with the title.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/answer_plot_consistency.py:384-397 compares each title against every `set_xscale`/`set_yscale` setter consistent with the state, not against the final effective scale, so an initialized-then-overridden axis is reported as a contradiction.

pr_title: serve: a request that outlives its process is recoverable (#418)
title: Exclude live requests before classifying checkpoints as recovered
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude live requests before classifying checkpoints as recovered**

When a chat request is running in this server, its lifecycle checkpoint is already present in the same history directory. This call discovers that checkpoint without checking live ownership, and the listing consequently includes both the live run and an `interrupted` recovery record claiming that its process is gone. I reproduced this with a live `UiState` run writing a checkpoint: the run remained `running` while recovery reported `no live owner`. Track the lifecycle request/session associated with live runs and exclude those checkpoints from recovery on both listing and status surfaces; otherwise normal in-flight work is incorrectly advertised as interrupted and safe to resume.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/server.py:1431 `recovered_requests()` calls `discover_requests(self.history_dir)` with no live-owner set; `discover_requests` (harness/run_recovery.py:141) classifies every checkpoint in the directory, and the status surface at :2130 merges live and recovered without excluding live request ids.

pr_title: serve: a request that outlives its process is recoverable (#418)
title: Honor the lifecycle's resumability flag for deferred requests
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor the lifecycle's resumability flag for deferred requests**

For a checkpoint with `status="deferred"`, the lifecycle persists `data.resumable` and sets `stage="terminal"`, but this branch treats any nonempty stage as resumable. Consequently, a deliberately non-resumable deferred request is advertised as resumable with instructions to resume its saved checkpoint, even though `LifecycleCoordinator.resume()` explicitly returns `None` when `data.resumable` is false. I reproduced this using a coordinator-created deferred checkpoint. Check the persisted deferred-state resumability flag rather than deriving resumability solely from the presence of a stage.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/run_recovery.py:55 keeps `deferred` in `_INTERRUPTED`, and :133 returns `resumable: bool(payload.get('stage'))`. The lifecycle persists its own `data.resumable` and sets stage `terminal` for deferred requests, so a deliberately non-resumable deferred request is still advertised as resumable.

pr_title: feat(state): separate local health, backend reachability and request state (#419
title: Probe the connected backend rather than a fresh local MCP process
body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Probe the connected backend rather than a fresh local MCP process**

When the desktop uses the remote `harness-oc` SSH transport, this default probe cannot detect its outage: `doctor.check_mcp_stdio()` launches a new local `python -m harness.mcp` subprocess instead of contacting the connected backend. The inspected verification record, `docs/audit/LAPTOP_LANE_VERIFY_2026-11-06.md`, explicitly records the local MCP smoke passing while the desktop's remote tunnel times out. In that documented failure scenario, the new component still reports `backend.state=ok` and treats requests as confirmed. Probe the configured transport, or report the connected backend as unknown when only local MCP startup has been checked.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/server.py:113 `_default_backend_probe()` returns `doctor.check_mcp_stdio`, which starts a fresh local `python -m harness.mcp` subprocess; it never contacts the configured `harness-oc` transport.

pr_title: feat(state): separate local health, backend reachability and request state (#419
title: Supply the configured MCP authentication token to the probe
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Supply the configured MCP authentication token to the probe**

When `mcp_auth_token` is configured, returning the bare doctor function causes the monitor to call `check_mcp_stdio()` without authentication. The spawned MCP server loads that token and rejects unauthenticated `tools/call` requests in `McpServer._authorize`, so its `ledger_status` check fails and a healthy backend is reported as unreachable. The existing doctor entry point passes `settings.mcp_auth_token` explicitly; bind the configured token here as well, independently of the UI authentication tokens.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/server.py:117 returns the bare `check_mcp_stdio` function, so the monitor probes without `settings.mcp_auth_token`; an MCP server that loads the token rejects the unauthenticated `tools/call` and a healthy backend reads as unreachable.

pr_title: feat(state): separate local health, backend reachability and request state (#419
title: Require request-specific evidence before marking a state confirmed
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require request-specific evidence before marking a state confirmed**

Whenever the generic backend probe succeeds, every recovered record is marked `confirmed`, even an unreadable checkpoint whose state is `unknown`. The production probe only checks MCP initialization, tool listing, and `ledger_status(limit=1)`; it never queries these request IDs or reconciles their states. Consequently, recovery of connectivity falsely upgrades stale local evidence to backend-confirmed request state. Keep confirmation false unless request-specific evidence was actually obtained, while preserving the independently reported backend reachability and durable checkpoint state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/state_report.py:198 sets `confirmed: reachable` for every record whenever the backend probe is OK, and the default probe asks only for MCP init, tool listing and `ledger_status(limit=1)`; no request id is ever queried.

pr_title: feat(ledger): signed reversible compaction replaces size-only eviction (#336)
title: Allow verification to cross consecutive signed drop runs
body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow verification to cross consecutive signed drop runs**

When adjacent eligible rows have different classification reasons, `_coverage_runs()` emits separate drop runs, but this check requires one run to span the entire gap between retained entries. For example, compacting `jev_eval → test-provenance offer → successful canary_probe → jev_eval` succeeds, yet a fresh loader reports verification failure at the second `jev_eval`. The omission is fully signed, but neither individual run matches both retained neighbors. Compose contiguous runs with matching hash boundaries so valid compaction does not break verification and block evidence export.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/ledger_compaction.py:431 `crosses_gap` requires one run with `first_seq == prev_seq + 1` and `last_seq == seq - 1`; `_coverage_runs` (:242) splits runs whenever the classification reason changes, so two contiguous signed runs across one gap cannot compose.
